diagnosis:
WHAT READS AS 'WESTERN' / 'TOO DETAILED' IN THE NEW OUTPUTS (vs the 1.5 originals and the real GO album pages)

1. Composition: picture vs chart. 1.5 puts the main subject directly on bare cream paper with a vignetted patch of ground and wide empty margins; insets are small ruled boxes sitting on the paper. gpt-image-2 / 2.5 paint a full-bleed rectangular PICTURE (sky gradient, horizon, one-point-perspective avenue, tiled comic-page panels edge to edge: see Sunburst mokykla, Sunburst miestas, g2 klubas). A painting with atmosphere is 'detailed artwork'; a figure on paper is a chart. The old lead's 'structured grid layout' is being read as comic panels, and 'botanical plate / engineering manual / realistic proportions' licenses fine naturalism.

2. Rendering idiom. 1.5: one even medium-weight dark-brown/charcoal ink outline around every figure and object, flat fills with ONE soft shadow tone, warm desaturated inks (dusty blue, olive, ochre-tan, oxblood red, grey-brown) on a greyish cream, visible paper grain. gpt-image-2 old prompt: fine coloured-pencil/hatched linework, thin lines, naturalistic value gradation. Sunburst old prompt: watercolour wash with no outlines, bokeh light-spots, glossy parquet reflections, chrome glints. Sunburst + A: outlines return, but in the flat mid-century AMERICAN commercial-art idiom (advertising/comic-book flat colour), which is the largest corpus of 'flat gouache + black outline + retro' the model knows. The real GO pages are neither: brush-and-ink line of variable weight, thin matte gouache/tempera washes, coarse offset screen, flat even diagram lighting, dull turquoise/ochre/olive/dusty-blue inks on dun paper.

3. People: this is the decisive 'Western' tell. 
   - Faces: new = symmetrical, slim-jawed, long-necked, doe-eyed magazine faces, smiling or gazing at a partner (Sunburst klubas, Sunburst+A gydytojas = 1950s US health-class poster with a pompadour and a pageboy). 1.5 = broad, heavy, square-jawed, strong cheekbones, slightly heavy-lidded, closed mouths, level neutral gaze often straight at the viewer: ID-photograph composure (gydytojas, seima, minia).
   - Bodies: new = slim, long legs, narrow waist, dancer proportions. 1.5 = stocky, thick-waisted, short-necked, square-shouldered, ordinary.
   - Poses: new = dynamic, interacting, ballroom holds, swing kicks, three-quarter views, warmth. 1.5 = static, catalogue stance, lined up in a row, frontal; even the dancers are a stiff shuffle.
   - Hair: new = bouffant, flips, glossy volume, 1950s-60s sets (paragraph A's 'short permed hair' produced exactly this). 1.5 = short, combed flat, side-parted men; flat practical bobs; cotton headscarves on older women.
   - Clothing: new = suit-and-tie, fitted bodices, full swing skirts to mid-thigh, heels, tailored fit: 'dressed up'. 1.5 = plaid flannel shirts, thick knit cardigans and sweaters, loose work jackets, straight knee-length dresses with a simple belt, heavy wool coats, flat shoes, cloth caps and headscarves; fabrics heavy and shapeless; colours brown, olive, dusty blue, oxblood, grey, mustard. The Soviet 1981 signal is cheap state-made cloth that fits loosely; the Western signal is tailoring.
   - Interiors & light: new = polished parquet with reflections, pendant lamps, atmospheric evening glow. 1.5 = flat even light, linoleum, bare painted plaster, a VIA band on a low plywood stage, a house-of-culture hall rather than a nightclub.
   - Density: new models add more figures, more props (plants, globes, extra buses), more texture everywhere; 1.5 leaves paper empty.
   - Objects/cars: both draw Zhiguli/Ikarus (the new models even add Gediminas tower and baroque Vilnius), so period OBJECTS are not the problem; the people and the rendering are.

4. Why paragraph A failed: it described the paint handling and clothing shapes generically ('flat gouache', 'black outlines', 'A-line dresses', 'permed hair', 'wool jackets'), which on a modern model resolves to the nearest big corpus: US mid-century advertising art. It never described FACES, BODY TYPE, POSTURE or fabric cheapness, which is where the 1.5 'Soviet' read actually lives, and it kept full-bleed picture composition. On gpt-image-2 it also over-flattened (owner: 'flat and austere'): the target has ONE soft shadow tone inside the outline, not pure flat colour.

5. Why 1.5 worked without being told: its prior for 'Soviet-era Lithuanian people' + 'wall chart' already produced plain stocky frontal types on paper. The newer models have a stronger fidelity/aesthetics prior, so these things must now be stated positively and concretely.

The three levers, in order of expected effect: (a) faces/bodies/posture/fabric stated concretely; (b) 'subject on bare paper' composition with vignetted ground; (c) print-production vocabulary (brush-ink line, one shadow tone, coarse offset screen, dun paper) in place of art-genre vocabulary.

Keep the three phrases he singled out verbatim; delete the phrases that license fine naturalism ('botanical plate / engineering manual', 'realistic proportions', 'structured grid layout') and the two negations; add the three things the new models lose by default: one even ink outline + one soft shadow tone, subject floating on bare paper with vignetted ground, plain sturdy frontal people. candidates.lead: An illustration for a Lithuanian-language learning flashcard, in the style of a late Soviet instructional wall chart / civil-defense (Grazhdanskaya Oborona) training poster, circa 1975-1985. This is an educational technical wall chart: economical poster draftsmanship with an even dark-brown ink outline around every figure and object, simple flat fills with one soft shadow tone, muted printing colors (dusty blue, olive, ochre-tan, brick red, warm grey) and an aged cream-paper offset-print feel with a faint coarse halftone. The bare cream paper is the background: the main subject stands directly on it with its patch of ground fading out at the edges, surrounded by wide empty margins, and the small inset panels sit on the paper as separate ruled boxes. Deadpan instructional calm throughout. Where people appear they are ordinary Soviet-era Lithuanian people of 1981: plain and sturdy, with broad unremarkable faces, closed-mouth neutral expressions and a level gaze, standing squarely in a period late-1970s setting.

questions: Softness: gpt-image-2 + paragraph A (gydytojas) came out flat and austere. Is 1.5's soft modelling INSIDE the ink outline part of the target, or would you accept the flatter GO-poster finish if the people and paper were right? Default assumed: 1.5's 'flat fill + one soft shadow tone' is the target; all three leads ask for that.

Composition: is 'subject floating on bare cream paper with a vignetted patch of ground' (1.5 miestas, mokykla, pjauti) a requirement, or are full-bleed picture panels (Sunburst+A mokykla) acceptable if the people and print finish are right? Default assumed: floating-on-paper is part of the look; all three leads ask for it.

Action cards: for verbs and scenes like klubas, is one stiff held position (GO procedure-diagram stiffness) acceptable in place of 1.5's looser movement? Default assumed: yes, stiffness is on-style. Tangent, one line only: the subject prose 'club hall' is itself a Western prime; 'house-of-culture hall with a small amateur band' would help klubas regardless of lead.
predictions:
F1 (cheapest change, lowest risk): should restore the floating-on-paper composition on gpt-image-2 and reduce fine hatching; on Sunburst it should cut the bokeh/gloss and bring outlines back. Weakest on faces and clothing glamour because the people description is still short; expect Sunburst people to be plainer than before but still prettier than 1.5. Risk: residual watercolour wash on Sunburst; gpt-image-2 may still draw sky-filled panoramas on place cards.

F2 (strongest pull toward the print finish): should give the most GO-authentic surface (dull inks, coarse screen, flat diagram light) on both 2.5 models and kill the reflective floors and glow. Risks: (a) 'printed page' and 'ruled boxes' may tempt caption text or a page number despite NO_TEXT_RULE; (b) the model may over-literalise the artefact (fold marks, stains, a tilted scan, visible paper edge) which fights the clean red bands; (c) if the model reads 'tempera wash' as loose painting it could get sketchier rather than crisper. People are described only generically here, so some Western face/body read may survive on Sunburst; F2 is the rendering hypothesis, not the people hypothesis.

F3 (most direct attack on 'Western'): should flip the people read on Sunburst (broad faces, thick-set bodies, flat hair, cardigans, flat shoes, linoleum) and remove the sock-hop energy from klubas. Risks: (a) over-literalisation into dour clone faces or near-caricature heaviness: watch minia and seima; (b) the long people block may crowd out the composition cue so full-bleed pictures persist; (c) 'identity-card photograph' could produce head-and-shoulders mugshot framing on person cards (gydytojas), which is actually close to 1.5 but may hurt verb cards; (d) the dress list may bleed onto professional/worker cards (a doctor in a cardigan under the white coat is fine; a doctor in plaid flannel is not).

Quality lever: worth ONE extra run of F1 on Sunburst at quality=low (cheap). Hypothesis: a smaller detail budget suppresses the fine naturalistic rendering and the extra props, which is a large part of 'too detailed'. Risk: mushier insets, worse hands, more text/flag errors; low quality is a blunt instrument, so treat it as a tie-breaker, not a primary lever. I would not test xhigh/max: more detail budget is the opposite of what the look wants.

If forced to bet: F3 beats F1 beats F2 on the owner's 'looks Western' criterion; F2 beats F3 beats F1 on 'looks like one 1981 printing'. The likely production lead is a splice: F3's people block on top of F2's print paragraph, trimmed to ~170 words, once the test shows which half carries more weight. Suggested test set per candidate: klubas (the Western stress test), gydytojas (faces), miestas (composition), pjauti (worker, action), seima (crowd of faces) = 5 cards x 3 candidates x 2 models = 30 images, under $1.
